## Walkthrough This PR centralizes control-plane topology lookup in monitor tests, threads the resulting topology into operator state-transition helpers (removing clientConfig from exception callbacks), adds single-node-aware skip logic in those helpers, and updates a machine-scale test to skip operator-violation assertions on single-node clusters. ## Changes **Topology-aware operator state transition testing** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Central topology fetch**
`pkg/monitortests/clusterversionoperator/legacycvomonitortests/monitortest.go`|Adds `e2e` logging; `EvaluateTestsFromConstructedIntervals` fetches control-plane `topology` and passes it into monitor test helpers instead of `w.adminRESTConfig`.| |**exceptionCallback signature change**
`pkg/monitortests/clusterversionoperator/legacycvomonitortests/operators.go`|`exceptionCallback` no longer accepts `clientConfig`; all callers and closures updated to the new signature.| |**Stable-system operator transition wiring**
`pkg/monitortests/clusterversionoperator/legacycvomonitortests/operators.go`|`testStableSystemOperatorStateTransitions` accepts `topology` and forwards topology/single-node info into `testOperatorStateTransitions`; internal exception closure updated.| |**Upgrade operator state transitions**
`pkg/monitortests/clusterversionoperator/legacycvomonitortests/operators.go`|`testUpgradeOperatorStateTransitions` accepts `topology`, derives `isTwoNode`, removes in-function topology lookup, updates exception closure signature, and passes topology/singleNode into `testOperatorStateTransitions`.| |**Core operator transition logic & single-node skips**
`pkg/monitortests/clusterversionoperator/legacycvomonitortests/operators.go`|`testOperatorStateTransitions` now takes `topology` and emits skipped JUnit cases for each operator/condition when topology == `SingleReplicaTopologyMode`; exception invocation updated to match removed param.| |**Upgrade progressing checks & single-node skips**
`pkg/monitortests/clusterversionoperator/legacycvomonitortests/operators.go`|`testUpgradeOperatorProgressingStateTransitions` accepts `topology`, derives `isTwoNode`, and adds explicit single-node skip messages for machine-config and Progressing=False per-operator checks.| |**Scale test topology-aware validation**
`test/extended/machines/scale.go`|AfterEach reloads kubeconfig, creates typed `configv1` client, retrieves control-plane topology via `exutil`, logs on error, and only asserts no operator `Progressing=False` violations when topology != `SingleReplicaTopologyMode`.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~45 minutes ## Possibly related PRs - [openshift/origin#31172](https://github.com/openshift/origin/pull/31172): Changes in the same `legacycvomonitortests/operators.go` area around topology-aware `Progressing`/exception handling for single-node clusters. - [openshift/origin#31112](https://github.com/openshift/origin/pull/31112): Refactors passing `topology` through `test*StateTransitions` and adjusts exception/skip handling for operator tests. ## Suggested labels `jira/valid-reference`, `ready-for-human-review` ## Suggested reviewers - sjenning - deads2k - p0lyn0mial
🚥 Pre-merge checks | ✅ 10 | ❌ 2 ### ❌ Failed checks (2 warnings) | Check name | Status | Explanation | Resolution | | :------------------------: | :--------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Docstring Coverage | ⚠️ Warning | Docstring coverage is 11.11% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. | Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold. | | Test Structure And Quality | ⚠️ Warning | PR introduces assertions without meaningful failure messages in scale.go AfterEach (lines 291-292 for topology retrieval failures) violating requirement `#4` for helpful diagnostic messages. | Add failure messages to assertions: `o.Expect(err).NotTo(o.HaveOccurred(), "failed to load config")` and `o.Expect(err).NotTo(o.HaveOccurred(), "failed to create configV1 client")` |
✅ Passed checks (10 passed) | Check name | Status | Explanation | | :----------------------------------------------: | :------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Title check | ✅ Passed | The title 'Skip CO condition tests on SNO' accurately and concisely describes the main objective of the changeset—skipping cluster operator condition tests on single-node OpenShift clusters, which is reflected consistently across all modified files. | | Linked Issues check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped because no linked issues were found for this pull request. | | Out of Scope Changes check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped because no linked issues were found for this pull request. | | Stable And Deterministic Test Names | ✅ Passed | All test names in modified files use stable, deterministic values with no dynamic information like timestamps or UUIDs found in test titles. | | Microshift Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | No new Ginkgo e2e tests added; PR modifies existing tests/helpers. Existing test has [apigroup:machine.openshift.io] tag providing MicroShift protection. | | Single Node Openshift (Sno) Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | No new Ginkgo tests (It, Describe, Context, When) were added in this PR. The changes only modify existing test infrastructure and helper functions to skip/handle SNO topology appropriately. | | Topology-Aware Scheduling Compatibility | ✅ Passed | PR modifies only test/monitoring code to skip tests on SNO and handle two-node topologies. No deployment manifests or problematic scheduling constraints are introduced. | | Ote Binary Stdout Contract | ✅ Passed | No process-level stdout writes violating OTE contract found. e2e.Logf writes to GinkgoWriter (exempted), logrus calls are in functions only, no direct klog or fmt.Print calls. | | Ipv6 And Disconnected Network Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | No new Ginkgo e2e tests are added. The PR modifies existing test helpers to add SNO topology awareness with no IPv4 assumptions or external connectivity requirements. | | Description Check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped - CodeRabbit’s high-level summary is enabled. |

I like the `topology` centralization in `EvaluateTestsFromConstructedIntervals`; that's better than a separate `getControlPlaneTopology` in each `test.*` function.

I'm fine with us making the call that we don't have capacity to monitor ClusterOperator behavior for single-node clusters.  I just think we want to make it clear that the motivation is lack-of-capacity, and not that we're saying that we think happy-case single-node updates having ClusterOperators go `Degraded=True` is a good thing.  For example, [the `Degraded` Godocs][1] say:

> Degraded indicates that the component (operator and all configured operands) does not match its desired state over a period of time resulting in a lower quality of service.

And in a world where we had infinite capacity, we would be able to teach all the cluster operators that a minute or whatever of downtime around a Node reboot or component update was expected single-node behavior, and not a quality-of-service miss.

Anyhow, no worries from me merging this, as long as the commit message and comments we're using to motivate the change are clearly saying "would be nice, but we don't have time" and aren't sounding like "even if we had infinite time, we wouldn't work on improving single-node ClusterOperator status".

[1]: https://github.com/openshift/api/blob/30525d574efa05f5236757228a2a519d1983ea7a/config/v1/types_cluster_operator.go#L174-L176
